description: This course explores the principles and techniques of perception and knowledge science, covering topics such as sensory data acquisition using cameras and microphones; feature extraction with techniques like SIFT and HOG; object recognition using deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch; knowledge representation through ontologies and semantic web technologies like RDF and OWL; reasoning systems including rule-based inference and probabilistic models such as Bayesian networks; natural language processing with algorithms like Word2Vec and BERT; knowledge discovery through data mining techniques such as clustering and association rule mining; and ethical considerations in AI systems including bias detection and mitigation strategies. The course emphasizes the integration of these concepts in real-world applications such as smart surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and intelligent tutoring systems.

clos.text: Define the fundamental concepts of perception and knowledge science, including sensory data acquisition, feature extraction, and object recognition.
Describe the architecture and operation of deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch for implementing perception algorithms.
Explain the principles and applications of knowledge representation techniques, including ontologies, RDF, and OWL for semantic modeling.
Apply natural language processing algorithms like Word2Vec and BERT to process and analyze textual data for knowledge extraction.
Evaluate the ethical implications of AI systems in perception and knowledge science, including bias detection and mitigation strategies.
